Through: Ms. Rupali  Bandhopadhya, ASC with  Mr. Abhijeet Kumar, Adv.
 SI Gajal Chugh, PS  Krishna Nagar.

CORAM:
 HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE AMIT MAHAJAN  ORDER % 09.07.2025 1.

The petitioners seek quashing of three FIRs being FIR Nos.306/2022 dated 25.06.2022,
524/2022 dated 02.12.2022 & 65/2023 dated 02.03.2023, all registered at Police Station Anand Vihar, for offences under Sections 354D/406/506/509/109/120B/201/34, 308/506/34 &
498A/406/34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 ('IPC'), respectively.
2. It is the case of the petitioners that three FIRs were registered at the instance of the complainant over the matrimonial dispute.

It is claimed that petitioner Mayank Tomar who was married to the complainant at the relevant time, separated from the complainant on 22.02.2022 and the complaint in regard to the first FIR under Section 354D was given belatedly on 25.06.2022.

3. Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that petitioners had filed a petition seeking quashing of the said FIR and after the notice was issued by this Court, another complaint was given by the complainant, which led to registration of the second FIR under Section 308 of the IPC alleging the incident dated 22.02.2022.
He submits that complaint in regard to the said incident was also given belatedly after almost 10 months of the incident and no MLC was ever conducted.
This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 11/07/2025 at 22:40:36 4.
He submits that to further harass the petitioners, the third FIR was got registered on a complaint given by the complainant on 02.03.2023 under Section 498A/406/420/34 of the IPC.

He submits that the incidents in all the three FIRs, even as per the complainant, relate to the period when she was staying with the petitioner Mayank Tomar in her matrimonial home and, therefore, three FIRs ought not to have been registered.
5. He further submits that the offence under Section 354D of the IPC even otherwise could not have been invoked against the family members being the husband and in-laws.
He submits that the Police erroneously also made the women accused for offence under Section 354D of the IPC whereas provision clearly mentions that only a man can be charged for such offence.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the complainant, on the other hand, states that the FIR was also registered in regard to offence under Section 509 of the IPC and the women of the house can also be made accused for such offences.

7. The perusal of the three FIRs, prima facie, indicates that the incidents relate to the alleged cruelty being subjected to the complainant while in a matrimonial relation for which three separate FIRs cannot continue.

8. Let an appropriate status report be filed in that regard before the next date of hearing.
9.
10. A copy of this order be placed in all the matters.

AMIT MAHAJAN, J JULY 9, 2025 "SK"
